pr_title: Allow certificate bundles for AIA fetching
pr_body:
AIA fetching can be be a single certificate, or it can be a "certs-only" CMS message, as defined in RFC5280:

> or a collection of certificates in a BER or DER encoded "certs-only" CMS message as specified in [[RFC2797](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2797)].

`Import` appears as-permissive as `new X509Certificate2(byte[])` for the single cert case, such as PEM. So I don't believe this is making a different scenario less permissive.

Closes #83366

Issue Details
### Description I have a certificate that is signed by Sectigo and one of the intermediary certs have an AIA entry of ``` Authority Information Access: CA Issuers - URI:http://crt.sectigo.com/SectigoPublicCodeSigningRootR46.p7c OCSP - URI:http://ocsp.sectigo.com ``` This URI is a PKCS 7 DER encoded file containing two certificates but the OpenSSL branch will call [OpenSslCertificateAssetDownloader.DownloadCertificate](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/2b185ac8c5c1302804a3336c62cb33782d9d4916/src/libraries/System.Security.Cryptography/src/System/Security/Cryptography/X509Certificates/OpenSslCertificateAssetDownloader.cs#L16-L40) to download the file at the AIA URI and then try and read the certificate with `new X509Certificate2(data)`. Unfortunately the `X509Certificate2` constructor is unable to open this certificate. it seems like OpenSSL does not support it altogether as it ends up failing on [OpenSslPkcsFormatReader.TryReadPkcs7](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/2b185ac8c5c1302804a3336c62cb33782d9d4916/src/libraries/System.Security.Cryptography/src/System/Security/Cryptography/X509Certificates/OpenSslPkcsFormatReader.cs#L220). When the AIA traversal code encounters this exception it stops and considers the chain to be complete and fails with `PartialChain - unable to get local issuer certificate`. ### Reproduction Steps A very simple reproducer of the problem at hand is. ```csharp using System; using System.IO; using System.Net.Http; using System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates; using System.Threading.Tasks; namespace AIATest; public static class Program { public static async Task Main(string[] args) { string downloadUri = "http://crt.sectigo.com/SectigoPublicCodeSigningRootR46.p7c"; HttpClient client = new(); HttpResponseMessage response = await client.GetAsync(downloadUri).ConfigureAwait(false); byte[] data = await response.Content.ReadAsByteArrayAsync().ConfigureAwait(false); // Fails here using X509Certificate2 cert = new(data); } } ``` To reproduce the error that occurs during the AIA traversal phase ```csharp using System; using System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates; namespace Hm. I can take a look to see what it would take to light up a P7B file - we'd also have to dig in to see how Windows and other platforms handle this. I (assume) this probably works in Windows.

> Hm. I can take a look to see what it would take to light up a P7B file

It already can be done by using X509Certificate2Collection and then calling Import. This is able to see both certificates in this specific p7b file. Unfortunately the code that does the AIA traversal uses just X509Certificate2 which does not work for this file.

> I (assume) this probably works in Windows.

It does, I just assumed it was because dotnet just uses Schannel to do all the AIA traversal work but I never looked too deeply.

> It already can be done by using X509Certificate2Collection and then calling Import

Yep.

> This is able to see both certificates in this specific p7b file. Unfortunately the code that does the AIA traversal uses just X509Certificate2 which does not work for this file.

We should just be able to change it to return an `X509Certificate2Collection` and import the whole collection to the `STACK_OF(X509)`:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/eb0b07b47e128fcff0e951470d29b68075c39c05/src/libraries/System.Security.Cryptography/src/System/Security/Cryptography/X509Certificates/OpenSslX509ChainProcessor.cs#L256-L270

In the case of a single certificate, we can create a collection that has just one certificate in it.

That's what I assumed would happen but wasn't sure how it would handle the cross signed certificates where one was a CA root in itself and the other was signed by a root. I'll try your draft PR though and see how if it works for my scenario. I appreciate the quick response. Happy to help in any other way.

I just tested your changes and unfortunately while it solves the problem with downloading and loading the AIA p7b file the validation does fail due to potentially the cross signed certs in that file. Using my `X509Chain` example in my post I now get

```
Failure RevocationStatusUnknown - unable to get certificate CRL
Failure OfflineRevocation - unable to get certificate CRL
Failure UntrustedRoot - self-signed certificate in certificate chain
```

Unfortunately when stepping through the code I think this problem now goes into OpenSSL and how it validates the provided certificates as it's the result (statusCode is `X509_V_ERR_SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN`) after https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/5683a5ab8fd6c5d60084c0b394e5f44e60a77d42/src/libraries/System.Security.Cryptography/src/System/Security/Cryptography/X509Certificates/OpenSslX509ChainProcessor.cs#L273-L274

Not sure if dotnet can do something about that as it's OpenSSL who isn't checking the cross signed cert and stopping immediately at the self signed one and not the one that is signed by a trusted CA.
Thanks for checking! That _sounds_ the same, if not similar, to the issue https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/43884.
Would you happen to have a public certificate that reproduces the issue? Don't need the private key for chain building.
